title: Lymphatic system
examples: How does the lymphatic system help fight infection?
What is the main difference between blood and lymph?
Where exactly do lymph nodes filter things from?

explain.say: Today we learn about the lymphatic system. It helps keep your body healthy.
First we look at tissue fluid. This fluid surrounds all your body's cells. It moves nutrients to the cells.
Next are lymph nodes. These small nodes filter the tissue fluid. They trap germs and foreign particles.
The fluid that collects in the vessels is called lymph. Lymph is filtered tissue fluid, not blood.
In the body, lymph fluid returns excess fluid to the bloodstream. This keeps blood volume stable.
In real life, think about a cut. The lymphatic system helps clean the wound. It removes debris and fights infection.

faq.q: What is the main difference between blood and lymph?
faq.a: Blood is the fluid in your blood vessels. Lymph is the fluid that has collected from the tissues. Lymph usually has fewer red blood cells than blood.
asks: Is lymph the same as blood?
What is the composition of lymph?

faq.q: Why do we have lymph nodes?
faq.a: Lymph nodes act like checkpoints for the body. They filter out any harmful substances or pathogens found in the tissues. They help keep you from getting sick.

faq.q: How does tissue fluid get into the lymphatic system?
faq.a: When fluid leaks out of capillaries into the tissues, it becomes tissue fluid. Some of this excess fluid enters the lymphatic capillaries to be processed.
asks: Where does the fluid for lymph come from?

faq.q: Does the lymphatic system have its own pump?
faq.a: No, it does not have a dedicated pump like the heart. Instead, muscle contractions and changes in pressure help move the lymph fluid along.
asks: How does lymph move through the body?

faq.q: What happens if the lymphatic system is damaged?
faq.a: If it is damaged, excess fluid can build up in the tissues. This condition is called edema, which causes swelling. It can also affect immune function.
asks: What is the effect of poor lymph drainage?
Can the body survive without it?

facts: Lymph fluid is mostly water, proteins, and immune cells.
Lymph nodes are concentrated in areas like the neck and armpits.
The lymphatic system drains excess interstitial fluid back to the blood.
Immune cells, like lymphocytes, mature and are activated within the nodes.

quiz.say: Which fluid is primarily responsible for filtering pathogens before they enter circulation?
quiz.why: Lymph nodes are specifically designed to trap and filter foreign particles from the tissue fluid.

wrong.1: Blood circulates through the heart and lungs, not primarily for filtering tissue fluid.
wrong.2: Tissue fluid is the general fluid surrounding cells; it is the material that gets filtered.
wrong.3: Capillaries are the tiny vessels that allow fluid exchange, but they do not perform the filtering action.

quiz.say: If the lymphatic system fails, what is the most likely immediate physical consequence?
quiz.why: The primary role of the system is to return excess fluid; failure leads to fluid accumulation, or edema.

wrong.0: Clotting is related to platelets and blood components, not the lymphatic drainage.
wrong.1: While swelling can affect pressure, the direct consequence of fluid backup is swelling, not necessarily low pressure.
wrong.3: Heart failure is related to the circulatory pump, not the lymphatic drainage system.

quiz.say: What is the composition of lymph fluid?
quiz.why: Lymph is derived from tissue fluid, so its main components are water and proteins, unlike plasma.

wrong.1: Lymph is generally low in red blood cells because they remain in the bloodstream.
wrong.2: It contains more than just electrolytes; it carries immune cells and proteins too.
wrong.3: This describes gas exchange, which happens in the alveoli, not the lymph fluid.
